The ceiling is a rookie who earns steady slot volume in a rising offense; the floor is the typical rookie slow start. Competition behind him is weak, which helps his path to snaps. A reasonable late-round upside dart.

jalen nailor.verdict: Consistent low-end producer capped as Raiders' SWR2
jalen nailor.report: Nailor has been remarkably steady but low — 103 then 101 pts, around 6 PPG both years — as a complementary piece. In Las Vegas he's the SWR2 behind Tre Tucker and rookie Jack Bech, limiting his ceiling. The floor is his established ~6 PPG role; the upside is modest unless targets consolidate. A depth flier rather than a difference-maker.

tre tucker.verdict: Ascending as the Raiders' clear WR1 — best floor/ceiling combo in this range
tre tucker.report: Tucker improved from 129 pts (7.6 PPG) to 162 (9.5 PPG) while earning the RWR1 role in Las Vegas on 92 targets plus 11 carries. As the top option in a thin room, his target share and gadget usage give him the highest floor here and real WR2 upside. The 8.7 weekly stdev signals boom-bust weeks, but the volume trend is the story. A genuine breakout candidate worth reaching for.

adonai mitchell.verdict: Talented but unproductive; LWR3 behind Garrett Wilson caps immediate role
adonai mitchell.report: Mitchell has yet to convert draft pedigree into production — just 88 pts (4.9 PPG) in 2025 on 74 targets shows efficiency problems. On the Jets he's the LWR3 behind Garrett Wilson, so the target path is congested. The ceiling is a third-year leap if the light comes on; the floor is more of the same inefficiency. Pure upside speculation at this cost.

rashod bateman.verdict: TD-dependent Raven whose 2025 crashed after a solid 2024
rashod bateman.report: Bateman swung from 175 pts (10.3 PPG) in 2024 to a dismal 55 (3.3 PPG) in 2025, largely because his production was touchdown-driven on modest volume. Behind Zay Flowers he's the clear #2 but on a run-heavy Ravens offense with limited targets to spread. The ceiling is a TD-fueled return to WR3 relevance; the floor is the 2025 collapse repeating. Tough playoff slate (@PIT, @CIN) adds risk.

jaylin noel.verdict: SWR4 buried in a deep Houston room — minimal current path
jaylin noel.report: Noel managed just 68 pts (4.0 PPG) as a second-year slot behind Nico Collins, Jayden Higgins, and Tank Dell. That SWR4 designation means his target floor is very low unless multiple injuries strike. The ceiling requires a role opening up in Houston's crowded rotation. A stash-only profile in deep leagues.

jack bech.verdict: Second-year LWR3 with minimal 2025 output — deep dart
jack bech.report: Bech's rookie-adjacent 2025 line (42 pts, 2.5 PPG on 29 targets) was negligible, and he sits as the LWR3 in Las Vegas behind Tucker and Nailor. The ceiling is a second-year jump if he climbs the depth chart; the floor is continued irrelevance. Low variance but also low output makes him a bench-only speculation. Not startable as drafted.

deebo samuel.verdict: Productive dual-threat but unsigned FA — undraftable until he lands
deebo samuel.report: Deebo remained productive in 2025 (188 pts, 11.1 PPG with 17 carries) leveraging his hybrid role, but as an unsigned free agent projected at 0 he can't be valued. His ceiling depends heavily on landing a scheme that uses his rushing and short-target versatility. The floor is a diminished role or committee spot in a new offense. Wait for a signing before drafting.

tre' harris.verdict: Low-variance rookie producer stuck as Chargers' RWR3
tre' harris.report: Harris posted a quiet 69 pts (4.1 PPG) with the lowest stdev in this group (2.9), reflecting a steady but tiny role. As the RWR3 behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, his path to volume is limited. The ceiling is a second-year step forward if he passes Johnston; the floor is continued low usage. A depth stash with a rough Week 17 (KC) playoff matchup.

isaac teslaa.verdict: Buried LWR3 in Detroit's loaded room — minimal opportunity
isaac teslaa.report: TeSlaa managed 76 pts (4.5 PPG) on just 27 targets as a rookie, and the LWR3 role behind Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams offers almost no target path. The ceiling requires injuries ahead of him in a high-powered offense; the floor is inactivity. Detroit's offense is good but the target hierarchy is set. Deep-league only.

ryan flournoy.verdict: Emerged to 6.7 PPG in 2025 but SWR3 behind Lamb/Pickens limits ceiling
ryan flournoy.report: Flournoy jumped from 18 pts as a rookie to 114 (6.7 PPG on 56 targets) in 2025, a real usage uptick. However, he sits as the SWR3 behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, capping his target floor in a crowded Dallas room. The ceiling is a flex-worthy stretch if injuries open snaps; the floor is a rotational role. A modest late-round upside piece.

brandon aiyuk.verdict: Injured (DNR) and now WR3 behind Evans/Pearsall — avoid until healthy
brandon aiyuk.report: Aiyuk's 2024 was already down (62 pts, 3.7 PPG) before his injury, and the DNR tag plus a projection of 0 signal serious health uncertainty. Even healthy, he's now the WR3 behind Mike Evans and Ricky Pearsall in San Francisco. The ceiling is a mid-season return to relevance if healthy; the floor is a lost season. Too risky to draft outside deep dynasty stashes.

cooper kupp.verdict: Aging slot on a new team, declining but with proven PPR floor if targeted
cooper kupp.report: Kupp slid from 175 pts (10.3 PPG) in 2024 to 116 (6.8 PPG) in 2025 as age and volume declined, and he's now the SWR3 in Seattle behind JSN and Shaheed. His low 4.2 stdev in 2025 shows a steady-but-modest floor when he plays. The ceiling is a bounce-back if he earns steady slot targets; the floor is age-related fade and injury risk. Veteran reliability edges him above pure darts.

malik washington.verdict: Ascending slot WR1 in Miami with Tyreek uncertain; clearest volume path in this tier
malik washington.report: Washington jumped from 3.2 PPG as a rookie to 6.9 in 2025 on 65 targets and 17 carries, showing rising trust and gadget usage. As the listed SWR #1 with Tyreek Hill a free agent, his target share could climb meaningfully in 2026, supporting the proj-106 ceiling. Floor is capped by low aDOT and a crowded young room (Bell, Wease, Reagor, Douglas), plus a tough Week 17 Bills matchup. Best combination of role certainty and upside among these deep darts.

tank dell.verdict: Big-play talent behind Nico, but serious knee injury and depth log-jam cloud 2026
tank dell.report: Dell posted 8.2 PPG on 81 targets in 2024 before a devastating knee injury wiped out 2025. The explosive-play upside is real if healthy, but he's listed as the #3 slot behind Nico Collins and rookie Jayden Higgins with Noel and Hutchinson also present. Questionable tag and a full year lost make the floor near-zero, while the ceiling depends entirely on recovery and Houston target concentration. A road wk16 PHI/wk17 GB playoff slate adds difficulty.

zachariah branch.verdict: Explosive rookie return man behind London; niche now, upside if role expands
zachariah branch.report: No NFL production yet as a rookie, but Branch profiles as a dynamic gadget/return threat listed as Atlanta's #3 slot behind Drake London. The ceiling case is a designed-touch role that grows as the season progresses; the floor is minimal fantasy relevance behind London and Zaccheaus. A soft wk15 @WSH / wk16 TB / wk17 NO playoff run is a plus if he earns snaps. Pure late-round lottery ticket on athleticism.

kayshon boutte.verdict: Steady back-to-back 120+ point seasons, but A.J. Brown arrival squeezes the ceiling
kayshon boutte.report: Boutte quietly delivered 122 and 124 PPR points the last two years at ~7.2-7.3 PPG with high weekly variance (7.3 stdev). The addition of A.J. Brown pushes him to the #3 role behind Brown and Doubs, denting his target floor. His ceiling is streamable WR4 spike weeks, but a brutal wk15 @KC playoff spot hurts. Reliable dart with a proven, if boom-bust, profile.

ja'kobi lane.verdict: High-upside Ravens rookie with real path to snaps behind Flowers
ja'kobi lane.report: No pro data yet, but Lane is listed as Baltimore's RWR #3 behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman, giving him a live path in a potent Lamar-led offense. The ceiling is a red-zone/vertical role that yields spike weeks; the floor is buried behind two established veterans. Proj 82 reflects genuine optimism for a rookie this deep. Late bye (wk13) then a tough divisional playoff slate (PIT/CIN) tempers the outlook.

xavier legette.verdict: Regressed as a sophomore; McMillan arrival buries him on the depth chart
xavier legette.report: Legette slid from 125 points as a rookie to 89 in 2025 (7.4 to 5.3 PPG) as efficiency cratered. Now listed as RWR #5 behind Tetairoa McMillan, Coker, and Metchie, his volume path looks thin. The ceiling requires injuries ahead of him; the floor is fantasy irrelevance. Draft capital keeps him rostered but the arrow points down.

jalen tolbert.verdict: Collapsed from 152 to 46 points; buried at LWR #5 in Miami
jalen tolbert.report: Tolbert cratered from a useful 8.9 PPG (79 targets) in 2024 to just 2.7 PPG on 34 targets in 2025. Now on Miami as the listed #5 outside receiver, the depth chart offers almost no clear path. Proj-90 feels aspirational; the realistic outcome is deep-bench filler with occasional spike weeks. Needs multiple injuries ahead of him to matter.

keon coleman.verdict: Former first-rounder stuck behind DJ Moore addition; boom-bust and TD-reliant
keon coleman.report: Coleman has hovered around 6 PPG both seasons (112 then 102 points) with high variance and heavy TD dependence in a Buffalo offense that spreads it around. The listed LWR #4 spot behind DJ Moore and Shakir caps his target ceiling. The upside is red-zone spikes with Josh Allen; the floor is weeks of single-digit output. Late-round upside swing more than a reliable contributor.

nick westbrook-ikhine.verdict: TD merchant whose 136-point 2024 crashed to 20 in 2025; new IND role uncertain
nick westbrook-ikhine.report: NWI's fantasy value is almost entirely touchdown-driven — 136 points in 2024 evaporated to 20 in 2025 when the scores dried up. Now the listed RWR #3 in Indianapolis behind Pierce and Downs, his proj-96 leans heavily on TD regression working in his favor. The ceiling is a double-digit-TD spike season; the floor is total irrelevance as we saw last year. Extremely volatile bet.

pat bryant.verdict: Second-year Bronco flashed as rookie but sits fourth in a crowded room
pat bryant.report: Bryant managed 4.4 PPG on 49 targets as a rookie, decent for a Day-2 pick, but is listed as SWR #4 behind Waddle, Sutton, Franklin, and Mims. The ceiling depends on injuries or a leap in year two; the floor is deep-bench stashing. Denver's offense can support a fourth option in spurts. Speculative developmental hold.

dontayvion wicks.verdict: Dropped to Philly's WR4; behind Smith and Brown with no clear volume
dontayvion wicks.report: Wicks fell from 111 to 76 points (6.5 to 4.5 PPG) as Green Bay's committee squeezed him, and now he's listed as Philadelphia's LWR #4 behind DeVonta Smith and Marquise Brown. The path to targets is thin on a run-leaning offense. His ceiling is occasional deep-shot spikes; the floor is waiver material. Depth-chart darkness dominates.

tory horton.verdict: Speedy Seahawk with big-play flashes but buried behind JSN, Shaheed, Kupp
tory horton.report: Horton showed vertical juice (6.9 weekly stdev) but only 22 targets and 3.8 PPG as a rookie. Listed RWR #4 behind Smith-Njigba, Shaheed, and Kupp, plus a Questionable tag, he needs injuries to see the field. The ceiling is explosive spike weeks in a Sam Darnold offense; the floor is inactive. Deep dynasty-flavored stash.

savion williams.verdict: Gadget athlete with minimal 2025 output; buried in deep Packers room
savion williams.report: Williams managed just 26 points (1.5 PPG) as a rookie despite 11 carries and 10 catches showing gadget intent. As GB's LWR #4 behind Watson, Reed, and Golden, standalone value is scarce. The ceiling hinges on designed-touch expansion in year two; the floor is negligible. Athletic upside dart only.

caleb douglas.verdict: Miami rookie fourth on the outside; pure developmental flyer
caleb douglas.report: No pro data and listed as Miami's RWR #4 behind Washington, Bell, and Wease, Douglas is a deep developmental hold. The ceiling requires an opportunity opening in a Tua-led passing offense; the floor is a redshirt-type season. Questionable tag adds early risk. Ignore in most redraft formats.

christian kirk.verdict: Veteran slot buried at WR5 in a jammed SF room; role has evaporated
christian kirk.report: Kirk's production has declined to 3.4 PPG (58 points) in 2025 as injuries and role loss piled up. Now listed as SF's SWR #5 behind Evans, Pearsall, Aiyuk, and Stribling, there's essentially no target path. The ceiling requires multiple injuries ahead; the floor is off the fantasy radar. Name value only at this ADP.

de'zhaun stribling.verdict: 49ers rookie fourth on depth chart; camp-body upside only
de'zhaun stribling.report: No NFL data, listed as SF's LWR #4 behind Evans, Pearsall, and Aiyuk in a crowded veteran room. Path to fantasy relevance is remote barring an injury cascade. The ceiling is spot starts late in the year; the floor is inactive. Deep watch-list name.

elijah sarratt.verdict: Ravens rookie behind Flowers, Bateman, and Lane; roster-clogged
elijah sarratt.report: Sarratt has no pro production and sits fourth in Baltimore's WR pecking order behind Flowers, Bateman, and fellow rookie Lane. The Ravens' run-heavy scheme limits WR volume beyond the top two. Ceiling is occasional deep-ball weeks; floor is irrelevance. Late bye (wk13) and tough playoff slate offer no bonus.

chris brazzell ii.verdict: Panthers depth WR with no depth-chart clarity; total dart throw
chris brazzell ii.report: No usable production data and no confirmed depth-chart role in Carolina behind McMillan, Coker, and Metchie. The ceiling requires a surprise camp rise; the floor is the practice squad. A wk15 CIN / wk16 @PIT / wk17 SEA playoff slate is unremarkable. Speculative only.

ted hurst iii.verdict: Tampa Bay deep flyer with no role or data; ignore in redraft
ted hurst iii.report: No production data and no Sleeper depth match in a Buccaneers room. Any fantasy relevance would require a major training-camp breakthrough. The ceiling is fringe spot-start weeks; the floor is off-roster. Purely a deep-dynasty name at this rank.

tyreek hill.verdict: Free agent with proj 0 and no team; landing spot dictates everything
tyreek hill.report: Hill's 218-point 2024 collapsed to 54 in 2025 on just 29 targets amid injury and a lost Miami role, and he enters 2026 as an unsigned free agent (proj 0). If he lands in a strong offense, the elite-speed ceiling remains real; if he stays unsigned or lands poorly, he's a zero. The Questionable tag and age-32 decline compound the uncertainty. Only draftable as a pure post-signing lottery ticket.

darius slayton.verdict: Steady WR2 behind Nabers but capped, low-target field-stretcher — bench flier only
darius slayton.report: Slayton posted 6.5 then 5.8 PPG across 2024-25 on 71 and 63 targets, a modest but stable role as the Giants' outside vertical option opposite Malik Nabers. His forward outlook is limited: with Nabers commanding volume and Mooney/Fields/Austin also in the mix, he's a TD-dependent complementary piece whose floor is barely startable. Ceiling comes on the occasional multi-catch deep game, but the low reception count in PPR keeps a lid on it. Playoff slate (CLE, @DET, @DAL) is neutral; questionable injury tag adds mild risk.

dyami brown.verdict: Buried at WR6 in Washington with declining production — waiver-wire fodder
dyami brown.report: Brown regressed from 4.0 PPG in 2024 to just 2.9 in 2025, and his depth-chart spot (#6 LWR) behind McLaurin, Williams, Lane and Jefferson signals a near-nonexistent projected role. His 37 targets and 20 catches offer almost nothing in PPR, and forward volume looks unlikely to grow given the crowded room. The only ceiling case is injuries ahead of him opening snaps. There's no reason to draft him in standard formats.

jahan dotson.verdict: WR4 in Atlanta with two straight sub-3-PPG seasons — deep-league dart at best
jahan dotson.report: Dotson has failed to launch since the trade, managing 2.5 then 3.0 PPG on tiny target shares (33, 36) and just 18-19 catches each year. Sitting #4 on Atlanta's chart behind London, Zaccheaus and rookie Branch, his forward path to relevant volume is blocked. Low weekly stdev confirms consistent irrelevance rather than boom potential. Only a raft of injuries would make him rosterable.

andrei iosivas.verdict: Bengals' WR3 with real red-zone upside behind Chase/Higgins — best contingent value here
andrei iosivas.report: Iosivas flashed a 7.1 PPG, 120-point line in 2024 before dipping to 5.3 in 2025, but he retains the highest ceiling of this group as Cincinnati's slot option in a pass-heavy, high-scoring offense. With Chase and Higgins drawing coverage, his target quality is strong, and any Higgins absence (a recurring risk) would spike his value into flex territory. Floor is a fringe bench role, but 58-61 targets over two years shows a real defined job. The playoff slate is friendly (@CAR, @IND) with a tougher BAL finish in Week 17.

trey mcbride.verdict: Elite target hog with league-winning ceiling; TE1 overall in PPR.
trey mcbride.report: McBride's 169 targets and 18.6 PPG in 2025 built on a strong 2024 (147 tgt, 14.7 PPG) confirm a genuine WR1-level workload from the TE spot. The ceiling is a scoring title given the volume; the floor stays high because he catches 120+ balls regardless of touchdown variance. Arizona's depth chart offers zero competition — Higgins and Reiman are afterthoughts, so the target funnel is secure. A clean bye (wk14) and manageable playoff slate (NYJ, @NO, LV) add to the appeal.

brock bowers.verdict: 2025 dip looks injury-driven; elite 2024 rookie form is the true baseline.
brock bowers.report: Bowers exploded as a rookie (153 tgt, 112 rec, 15.5 PPG) before a down 2025 (86 tgt, 10.4 PPG) that the high 10.5 stdev suggests was disrupted by injury or missed usage. The ceiling matches McBride's if healthy given his target-magnet role, and Vegas has no real TE competition behind him. The floor carries more risk than McBride because of the volatile 2025 and QB uncertainty. Playoff schedule (DEN, TEN, @ARI) is fine.

colston loveland.verdict: Ascending sophomore with rookie production and clear runway in Chicago.
colston loveland.report: Loveland flashed as a rookie with 82 targets and 9.7 PPG, a strong Year 1 foundation pointing to a Year 2 leap. The ceiling is a top-five finish if the Bears' passing game funnels through him; the floor is muted by the presence of Cole Kmet still stealing snaps and touches. His target share should grow, but the two-TE setup caps his workhorse potential. A tough wk15 (@BUF) is offset by GB and DET at home to close.

tyler warren.verdict: Ultra-consistent rookie (4.7 stdev) with 112 targets and a locked-in role.
tyler warren.report: Warren's rookie line — 112 targets, 76 rec, 11.1 PPG with a remarkably low 4.7 weekly stdev — makes him one of the safest young TEs in the pool. The floor is elite for the position because he sees volume every week; the ceiling depends on Indy's overall offensive efficiency and red-zone looks. He owns the Colts TE room outright with only Alie-Cox behind him. Playoff slate (@TEN, CIN, @CLE) is neutral.

harold fannin jr..verdict: Productive rookie with 107 targets; upside tied to a shaky Cleveland offense.
harold fannin jr..report: Fannin posted 107 targets and 11.0 PPG as a rookie, a genuine breakout foundation with modest 6.0 stdev consistency. The ceiling is a mid-range TE1 if Cleveland's QB play stabilizes; the floor is dragged down by one of the league's weakest passing environments. His depth chart is unclear but he clearly earned volume last year. Playoff matchups (@NYG, @BAL, IND) are mixed with a tough Baltimore game.

kyle pitts sr..verdict: Finally delivered a real season (12.4 PPG, 118 tgt); breakout at last.
kyle pitts sr..report: Pitts nearly doubled his 2024 output (7.7 to 12.4 PPG) with 118 targets in 2025, the long-awaited season that matches his talent. The ceiling is top-five if Atlanta keeps feeding him; the 9.6 stdev signals boom-bust weeks that hurt the floor. No meaningful TE competition on the depth chart secures his role. Playoff slate (@WSH, TB, NO) is favorable.

sam laporta.verdict: Talent is real but 2025 collapse (6.3 PPG) and injury tag cloud the outlook.
sam laporta.report: LaPorta cratered from 10.3 PPG (2024) to just 6.3 on only 49 targets in 2025, a steep usage drop in a crowded Detroit offense. He carries a Questionable injury tag that raises games-missed risk. The ceiling is a rebound toward his rookie form if the offense re-prioritizes him; the floor is ugly given the target erosion. Bye wk6 with a decent playoff run (@MIN, NYG, @CHI).

travis kelce.verdict: Steady 11+ PPG floor at 13 years but age caps ceiling; reliable TE2 value.
travis kelce.report: Kelce held serve with 108 targets and 11.4 PPG in 2025, nearly identical to 2024, showing he's still a volume anchor in KC. The floor is safe thanks to consistent target share and low-ish 6.2 stdev; the ceiling is limited by age-related decline in explosiveness. He remains the unquestioned KC TE1 with only Noah Gray behind. Playoff schedule (NE, SF, @LAC) is playable.

george kittle.verdict: Elite when healthy but 2025 dip and injury tag temper the projection.
george kittle.report: Kittle fell from 13.9 PPG (2024) to 9.5 in 2025 with reduced targets (69) and a high 9.5 stdev, and he carries a Questionable tag. The ceiling remains among the highest at the position given his big-play ability on a good offense; the floor is soft due to injury and volume risk. He's the clear SF TE1 with no threat behind him. Bye wk8, playoff slate (@LAC, @KC, PHI) leans tough.

dallas goedert.verdict: Bounce-back 2025 (10.9 PPG) but low-volume Philly offense caps ceiling.
dallas goedert.report: Goedert nearly doubled his output from 2024 (6.1) to 10.9 PPG in 2025 on 82 targets, a solid rebound. The ceiling is capped by Philadelphia's run-heavy, spread-the-ball approach; the floor is stable when healthy but he's missed time historically. He leads a thin TE room with only Stowers and Calcaterra behind. Playoff schedule (SEA, HOU, @SF) is average.

jake ferguson.verdict: Big 2025 rebound (11.1 PPG, 102 tgt) on high-volume Dallas passing game.
jake ferguson.report: Ferguson surged from 6.1 to 11.1 PPG in 2025 with 102 targets and 82 receptions, thriving as a reliable underneath option. The ceiling is a low-end TE1 if Dallas keeps throwing at volume; the moderate 6.9 stdev gives a reasonable floor. He owns the Cowboys TE job with no real competition. A late bye (wk14) and soft playoff slate (@LAR, JAX, NYG) are pluses.

tucker kraft.verdict: 2025 fell off (6.9 PPG) and Questionable tag; volatile rebound bet.
tucker kraft.report: Kraft dropped from 9.6 PPG (2024) to 6.9 in 2025 on just 44 targets with a very high 9.7 stdev, signaling boom-bust and reduced usage. He carries a Questionable injury tag that adds games-missed risk. The ceiling is a rebound if Green Bay concentrates targets, but Musgrave lurks in a committee. Playoff slate (MIA, @CHI, HOU) is neutral.

isaiah likely.verdict: New team (NYG) gives a fresh shot after buried 2025 role in Baltimore.
isaiah likely.report: Likely's 2025 was minimal (3.6 PPG, 37 tgt) behind Andrews, but a move to the Giants as their TE1 opens a path to volume. The ceiling is a low-end starter if he wins the target share over Theo Johnson; the floor is low given an unproven QB situation and his own inconsistent track record. His 2024 (7.3 PPG) shows some upside when involved. Playoff slate (CLE, @DET, @DAL) is mixed.

t.j. hockenson.verdict: Low-ceiling steady option; 6.6 PPG floor in a crowded Minnesota offense.
t.j. hockenson.report: Hockenson managed just 6.6 PPG on 66 targets in 2025, an underwhelming return from a talent who's fought injuries. The low 4.4 stdev gives a predictable but modest floor; the ceiling requires a target-share jump that Jefferson, Addison and the RBs make unlikely. He's the clear TE1 with Josh Oliver as a blocker behind. Playoff slate (DET, WSH, @NYJ) is reasonable.

kenyon sadiq.verdict: Rookie lottery ticket on NYJ with a Questionable tag and no track record.
kenyon sadiq.report: Sadiq enters as a rookie with zero NFL data and a Questionable injury tag, making him a pure projection play at ADP 148. The ceiling is a surprise rookie contributor if he beats out Mason Taylor for the lead role; the floor is near-zero fantasy value if he sits behind veterans. The depth chart is genuinely contested with Taylor and Ruckert. Late bye (wk13) and a fine playoff slate matter little given the uncertainty.

mark andrews.verdict: Sharp 2025 decline (7.7 PPG) at age 30+; TD-dependent, fading role.
mark andrews.report: Andrews slid from 11.1 to 7.7 PPG in 2025 even with 10 rushing attempts padding his line, a clear downtrend as Baltimore diversifies. The ceiling relies heavily on red-zone touchdowns given his shrinking target base; the floor is low if the scores dry up. He's still the nominal TE1 but the volume trend is worrisome. Playoff slate (@PIT, CLE, @CIN) is tough.

dalton kincaid.verdict: Modest 2025 (7.4 PPG); low-volume Buffalo passing game limits upside.
dalton kincaid.report: Kincaid improved slightly to 7.4 PPG in 2025 but on just 49 targets, reflecting Buffalo's spread-the-wealth attack. The ceiling is a matchup-based streamer if the target share grows; the floor is low given how few looks he commands. Knox and Hawes chip into the TE snaps. Playoff slate (CHI, @DEN, @MIA) is playable.

hunter henry.verdict: Quietly consistent 10.5 PPG in 2025; safe low-end streamer at 30+.
hunter henry.report: Henry posted a solid 10.5 PPG on 87 targets in 2025, up from 8.6 in 2024, showing steady involvement in New England's offense. The floor is dependable given his volume and 7.1 stdev; the ceiling is capped by age and touchdown reliance. He faces no real TE competition on the depth chart. Playoff slate (@KC, @NYJ, DEN) is a bit tough for the finish.

terrance ferguson.verdict: Buried rookie (3.1 PPG) behind a crowded LAR TE room; deep flier only.
terrance ferguson.report: Ferguson barely registered as a rookie (25 tgt, 11 rec, 3.1 PPG) and sits atop a genuinely crowded Rams TE depth chart with Parkinson and Higbee. The ceiling requires a major Year 2 leap and target consolidation that isn't guaranteed; the floor is near-irrelevant fantasy production. This is a dynasty/upside stash more than a redraft asset. Playoff slate (DAL, @SEA, @TB) doesn't move the needle.

juwan johnson.verdict: Career-best 2025 (10.6 PPG, 102 tgt) but Fant addition threatens role.
juwan johnson.report: Johnson broke out in 2025 with 102 targets and 10.6 PPG at a very consistent 4.7 stdev, the best season of his career. The concern is the arrival of Noah Fant, which could split the TE targets and cap his 2026 volume. The ceiling is a repeat low-end TE1 if he holds the job; the floor drops if New Orleans' offense and QB play crater. Playoff slate (@TB, ARI, @ATL) is neutral.

brenton strange.verdict: Undisputed JAX TE1 on a two-year upward arc with a clear target floor
brenton strange.report: Strange bumped from 5.4 to 6.9 PPG and 53 to 60 targets year-over-year, and at just 3 years experience the arrow points up with a soft same-team depth chart (Boerkircher, Koziol) offering no threat. The ceiling case is a full-time role expanding toward 80+ targets and low-end TE1 numbers, matching his aggressive 142 projection. The floor is the modest but stable 6-7 PPG line he already posted, with low weekly variance (stdev 5.9). Playoff slate (@HOU, @DAL, WSH) is neutral; he's a reliable late-round streamer.

dalton schultz.verdict: 106-target 2025 makes him the safest floor in this tier if volume holds
dalton schultz.report: Schultz exploded to 10.5 PPG on 106 targets in 2025, nearly doubling his 2024 output and pacing this entire group in usage. The ceiling is a repeat top-8 finish given his entrenched HOU role and 82 catches; the floor is a regression toward his 2024 7.0 PPG if targets bleed back to the WRs. At 8 years experience the age/decline clock ticks, but no same-team TE (Klein, Moreau) threatens his role. Neutral playoff draw (JAX, @PHI, @GB); a strong volume-based value here.

pat freiermuth.verdict: 2025 crash from 168 to 114 pts clouds him, but a bounce-back is live
pat freiermuth.report: Freiermuth's production tumbled from 9.9 PPG and 78 targets in 2024 to 6.7 PPG and 54 targets in 2025 amid PIT's offensive turnover. The ceiling is a return to that 2024 form if the passing game stabilizes and he reclaims red-zone looks; the floor is the diminished 2025 line repeating. Washington's growing role is a genuine target competitor within the room. Playoff schedule (BAL, CAR, @TEN) is manageable; a boom-or-modest streamer.

chig okonkwo.verdict: New WSH home with 79 targets in 2025 and elite low-variance consistency
chig okonkwo.report: Okonkwo posted 7.3 PPG on 79 targets with a tiny 4.3 weekly stdev, one of the steadiest floors in this pool across both seasons. The move to Washington's offense offers ceiling if he becomes a featured underneath outlet, though Sinnott lurks as a developing same-team option. The floor is his proven 6.7-7.3 PPG baseline. Playoff slate (ATL, @MIN, @JAX) is fine; a dependable, low-drama TE2/streamer.

aj barner.verdict: Doubled his output to 8.7 PPG with rushing usage, but injury tag caps confidence
aj barner.report: Barner leapt from 4.6 to 8.7 PPG and added 10 carries, showing real red-zone and rushing involvement in SEA's scheme. The ceiling is continued TD-driven upside with growing targets; the floor is dragged down by the Questionable injury tag and the emergence of Elijah Arroyo threatening snaps. Weekly variance (6.3) reflects TD-dependence. Tough Week 15 (@PHI) but overall a fine bet if healthy.

gunnar helm.verdict: Year-2 rookie ascender as TEN's clear TE1 with a clean depth chart
gunnar helm.report: Helm delivered 5.4 PPG on 55 targets as a rookie with very low variance (stdev 4.0), and at just 1 year experience he offers the classic second-year leap profile. The ceiling depends on TEN's offense improving and his target share climbing past 70; the floor is the quiet rookie baseline repeating. Depth chart (Bellinger, Granson) poses no threat to his lead role. Neutral playoff draw; a speculative upside stash.

oronde gadsden.verdict: Explosive rookie flashes but Njoku's arrival muddies the LAC target picture
oronde gadsden.report: Gadsden's 7.7 PPG on 69 targets as a rookie came with the highest variance in the group (stdev 7.4), signaling boom-bust weeks. The ceiling is a true breakout if he holds the featured role; the major risk is David Njoku joining the room and splitting looks in a crowded LAC passing game. Tough playoff opener (SF) and a KC finish add scheduling concern. High-ceiling gamble with real touch-competition downside.

cade otton.verdict: Proven TB volume but 2025 dip and Culp's presence trim the outlook
cade otton.report: Otton logged 81 targets and 7.2 PPG in 2025, down from 8.3 the prior year, showing a steady if unspectacular floor. The ceiling is a return toward that 8+ PPG range if TB leans on him again; the floor reflects his declining efficiency and rising weekly variance (6.0). No serious same-team threat, but the projection (102) is the lowest among the starters here. Favorable playoff finish (NO, @ATL, LAR) is a mild plus.

evan engram.verdict: New DEN home and 76 targets keep him relevant despite age
evan engram.report: Engram drew 76 targets for 6.0 PPG in 2025 with tight variance (stdev 4.0), a PPR-friendly high-volume, low-yardage profile. The ceiling is a bump if Denver features him as a possession outlet; the floor is age-related fade at 9 years experience with no TD spikes. Depth chart is clear, so touches aren't threatened. Tough Week 16 (BUF); a safe-floor, capped-ceiling streamer.

mike gesicki.verdict: 2025 collapse to 4.2 PPG makes him a pure bounce-back dart throw
mike gesicki.report: Gesicki cratered from 8.3 PPG and 83 targets in 2024 to 4.2 PPG and 42 targets in 2025 as CIN's passing distribution shifted. The ceiling is a full rebound to 2024 usage if health and target share return; the floor is the ugly 2025 line, with Erick All also competing for looks. High variance (5.2) on low volume is a red flag. Speculative upside only.

greg dulcich.verdict: 6.3 PPG in a 10-game sample; MIA TE1 with injury and role questions
greg dulcich.report: Dulcich managed 6.3 PPG on 33 targets over just 10 games in 2025, his lone real production sample given no 2024 data. The ceiling is a fully healthy season as Miami's lead TE pushing toward 60 targets; the floor is games-missed risk and an unproven full-season workload. Depth chart is soft, so opportunity exists if he stays on the field. Rough playoff bookends (@GB, BUF); a lottery ticket.

david njoku.verdict: Fell off a cliff in 2025 and now projects behind Gadsden in LAC
david njoku.report: Njoku plummeted from 8.7 PPG and 97 targets in 2024 to 5.1 PPG in 2025, and the LAC depth chart lists him as TE2 behind breakout rookie Gadsden. The ceiling requires him to reclaim the lead role, which the projection (85) doesn't buy; the floor is a timeshare afterthought. At 9 years experience with declining usage, the trend is bleak. Only draftable if you believe the veteran wins the job outright.

michael mayer.verdict: Buried behind Brock Bowers; touches simply aren't there
michael mayer.report: Mayer's 4.3 PPG on 50 targets in 2025 improved on his dismal 2024 but caps out low as the clear TE2 behind elite Brock Bowers. The ceiling is injury-contingent standalone value; the floor is near-irrelevance in most weeks. No path to volume exists while Bowers is healthy. A deep-league handcuff at best.

jake tonges.verdict: Kittle backup with a Questionable tag and a 33-point projection
jake tonges.report: Tonges posted 5.5 PPG in 2025 but sits firmly as SF's TE2 behind George Kittle, and the 33-point projection reflects minimal expected snaps. The ceiling only opens if Kittle misses time, at which point his high variance (6.6) hints at usable spike weeks. The floor is essentially zero fantasy relevance. His own Questionable tag compounds the risk; a pure handcuff dart.

josh allen.verdict: The unquestioned QB1 — elite dual-threat floor and ceiling, 100+ carries every year
josh allen.report: Allen posted 22.3 then 21.4 PPG across the last two seasons with a rock-solid 17-game track record and 100+ carries annually, the rushing floor that separates elite QBs. His 369 projection tops the position and his weekly stdev (11-12) reflects boom weeks rather than duds. Floor case is a top-3 finish; ceiling is the overall QB1 crown. No real threat behind him with Buechele/Allen as backups, and the wk15-17 slate (CHI, @DEN, @MIA) is manageable.

lamar jackson.verdict: 430-point 2024 ceiling is league-winning, but the 2025 collapse to 12.6 PPG is a real flag
lamar jackson.report: Jackson's 2024 (25.3 PPG, 430 total, absurd 6.0 stdev) was the best fantasy QB season in years, but 2025 cratered to 12.6 PPG with rushing carries halved to 67 — a warning that his production hinges on health and mobility. The ceiling case matches or beats Allen; the floor case is what we saw last year. If the legs are back he's a set-and-forget QB1. Playoff draw (@PIT, CLE, @CIN) is division-heavy and tough.

jayden daniels.verdict: Elite rookie rushing floor (148 car in 2024) makes him a QB1 if healthy after 2025 washout
jayden daniels.report: Daniels' 2024 rookie year (20.9 PPG, 148 carries) showcased the rushing volume that gives QBs a sky-high fantasy floor, but 2025 collapsed to 6.7 PPG — almost certainly injury-driven given the same team and role. The ceiling is a top-5 finish built on legs; the floor is another lost season. No competition behind him with Mariota as QB2. Bounce-back is the bet, and the rushing profile makes it worth it at this ADP.

drake maye.verdict: Legit breakout — 20.7 PPG with a tiny 5.2 stdev and 103 carries signals a weekly steady QB1
drake maye.report: Maye leaped from 10.4 PPG as a 2024 rookie to 20.7 in 2025 with an exceptionally low 5.2 weekly stdev — the most consistent QB profile in this group — plus 103 carries for a rushing floor. That consistency is his selling point: he rarely busts, giving a strong floor with a low-end QB1 ceiling. No competition on the depth chart. The playoff slate is rough (@KC, @NYJ, DEN all tough defenses), the main knock on an otherwise clean ascending profile.

jalen hurts.verdict: TD-dependent tush-push floor keeps him a steady QB1 despite modest passing volume
jalen hurts.report: Hurts delivered 18.5 then 17.6 PPG with 150 and 105 carries, his rushing near the goal line providing a reliable TD floor even in a run-first Eagles offense. The ceiling is capped by low passing volume, but the floor is dependable and he plays 17 games. No depth-chart concern behind him. His 320 projection reflects a safe QB1 with limited upside; playoff matchups (SEA, HOU, @SF) are middling.

joe burrow.verdict: Elite passing ceiling (373 in 2024) but 2025 injury dropped him to 7.9 PPG — health is everything
joe burrow.report: When healthy in 2024 Burrow was a top-3 fantasy QB at 21.9 PPG, but 2025 was wrecked by injury (7.9 PPG). With no rushing to fall back on, his floor is entirely tied to staying upright, and the injury history is now a pattern. The ceiling with Chase and Higgins is one of the highest in the league. His wk15-16 playoff draw (@CAR, @IND) is soft and could carry a title team.

jaxson dart.verdict: Mobile second-year passer with 86 carries and QB2 upside as a cheap late flier
jaxson dart.report: Dart's debut season produced 14.2 PPG with 86 carries, a mobile profile that gives him fantasy relevance beyond his passing. The high 11.1 stdev reflects a boom-bust rookie; a year-two leap is plausible with the rushing floor. He's the clear starter with only Winston behind him. Ceiling is a back-end QB1 in a good week; floor is streamer territory. Playoff schedule (CLE, @DET, @DAL) is mixed.

matthew stafford.verdict: Bounced back to 20.6 PPG in 2025 with elite weapons — quietly a value at this ADP
matthew stafford.report: Stafford rebounded from a down 2024 (12.6) to 20.6 PPG in 2025 with a low 6.8 stdev, a consistent pocket passer feeding an elite receiving corps. At age-37 the decline risk is real and he offers zero rushing, capping the floor. But the volume and efficiency give a low-end QB1 ceiling at a QB2 price. Playoff draw (DAL, @SEA, @TB) is manageable.

brock purdy.verdict: Efficient when the offense is healthy but 2025 slid to 10.4 PPG with a volatile 12.1 stdev
brock purdy.report: Purdy dropped from 15.7 PPG in 2024 to 10.4 in 2025 with a high 12.1 stdev, reflecting an offense hit by injuries around him. His ceiling depends entirely on his skill-position weapons being healthy; his floor is low given minimal rushing. He's the clear starter but a matchup-based streamer. The playoff slate (@LAC, @KC, PHI) is difficult.

dak prescott.verdict: Healthy 2025 (18.5 PPG) shows QB1 upside, but injury tag and no legs cap the range
dak prescott.report: Prescott's 18.5 PPG in a full 2025 was a return to form after an injury-shortened 2024 (6.9), and the low 8.0 stdev is encouraging. With no rushing and a Questionable tag, his floor is fragile. The ceiling with CeeDee Lamb and Dallas's passing volume is a solid low-end QB1. Playoff matchups (@LAR, JAX, NYG) are neutral-to-favorable.

trevor lawrence.verdict: Big 2025 leap to 19.9 PPG with 82 carries — an ascending streamer with QB1 weeks
trevor lawrence.report: Lawrence jumped from 8.5 PPG in 2024 to 19.9 in 2025, adding a useful 82 carries that lifts his floor. The improved efficiency and rushing suggest a genuine step forward, offering back-end QB1 upside. Floor is streamer level if the passing regresses. No depth-chart concern; playoff draw (@HOU, @DAL, WSH) is a mixed bag.

caleb williams.verdict: Improved to 18.7 PPG with 77 carries — a rising dual-threat with modest weekly variance
caleb williams.report: Williams climbed from 15.0 to 18.7 PPG in year two with 77 carries and a stable 8.0 stdev, a promising trajectory for a young mobile QB. The rushing gives him a QB2-plus floor and a back-end QB1 ceiling as the offense matures. No competition behind him. The playoff slate is brutal though (@BUF, GB, DET), a real drag on his title-week value.

bo nix.verdict: Two straight ~18 PPG seasons with 80+ carries — reliable QB2 floor, health tag to watch
bo nix.report: Nix has been remarkably steady at 18.7 then 17.9 PPG with 83-92 carries and a low stdev, a dependable dual-threat profile. The rushing volume gives him a solid floor, but the ceiling is capped and he carries a Questionable tag. He's a fine matchup streamer with QB1 weeks. The playoff schedule (@LV, BUF, @NE) mixes one great and one tough draw.

patrick mahomes.verdict: Steady ~16.7 PPG the last two years — name value exceeds current fantasy ceiling
patrick mahomes.report: Mahomes has settled into 16.6-16.8 PPG, a fine real-life QB but merely a mid-QB2 in fantasy without gaudy passing numbers or heavy rushing. The 60+ carries add modest floor support, but a Questionable tag and Fields lurking add mild noise. Ceiling remains high if KC's passing volume spikes; floor is a safe streamer. Playoff draw (NE, SF, @LAC) is neutral.

justin herbert.verdict: Ultra-consistent ~16.8 PPG with 80 carries — dependable QB2 with limited upside
justin herbert.report: Herbert has been metronomic at 16.8-16.9 PPG across both seasons with a low stdev and a useful 80+ carries that support his floor. The consistency makes him a safe streamer, but the ceiling is muted by conservative game scripts. No depth-chart threat. Playoff slate (SF, @MIA, KC) is manageable.

jared goff.verdict: Steady 17.5 PPG pocket passer but zero rushing hard-caps the ceiling
jared goff.report: Goff produced 17.5 PPG in 2025 with elite weapons but a near-total lack of rushing (19 carries) leaves no floor cushion when TDs dry up. The ceiling is a back-end QB1 in a shootout; the floor is a low-end streamer. He's entrenched as the starter. Playoff schedule (@MIN, NYG, @CHI) is neutral. Fine as a late QB2 but nothing more.

baker mayfield.verdict: Dropped from 21.5 to 16.0 PPG in 2025 — regression risk with no rushing safety net
baker mayfield.report: Mayfield fell from a career 21.5 PPG in 2024 to 16.0 in 2025, and with only modest rushing his floor rests on passing efficiency. The 6.1 stdev is stable but the downward trend and TD-dependence are concerns. Ceiling is a low-end QB1 if the 2024 form returns. Playoff draw (NO, @ATL, LAR) is favorable, a small plus.

tyler shough.verdict: Rookie-year 9.3 PPG with modest rushing — deep-league dart throw only
tyler shough.report: Shough's debut produced just 9.3 PPG, streamer-floor territory, though the 45 carries hint at some rushing upside if he develops. Competition from Rattler for the job adds uncertainty. The ceiling is a year-two leap into QB2 relevance; the floor is a bench arm. Playoff matchups (@TB, ARI, @ATL) are mixed. Only for the deepest leagues.

kyler murray.verdict: 2025 collapse to 4.6 PPG plus a move to MIN with McCarthy behind him — huge risk
kyler murray.report: Murray's 2025 was a disaster at 4.6 PPG after a solid 17.5 in 2024, and the reported move to Minnesota with J.J. McCarthy as QB2 injects real job-security risk. The ceiling if he wins the job and rushes like 2024 (78 carries) is a QB2; the floor is a bench outcome. This is a bet on volatility. Playoff slate (DET, WSH, @NYJ) is neutral.

daniel jones.verdict: 13.3 PPG in 2025 but Questionable tag and Richardson lurking make the job shaky
daniel jones.report: Jones bounced to 13.3 PPG in 2025 with some rushing (45 carries), a serviceable streamer level, but a Questionable tag and Anthony Richardson behind him threaten his hold on the job. The ceiling is a matchup-based QB2; the floor is a benching. He offers little for standard leagues. Playoff draw (@TEN, CIN, @CLE) is mixed.

jordan love.verdict: Two straight 13.8 PPG seasons plus rushing floor make him the safest streamer target here
jordan love.report: Love posted identical 235 and 234 point seasons (13.8 PPG) with rising rushing volume (25 to 47 carries), so his 259 projection reflects a stable, ascending profile. Ceiling case is a full-season 18+ PPG stretch if the GB pass game clicks, floor is his reliable low-double-digit output backed by legs. No real QB competition (Tyrod, McCord behind him) means workhorse security. Playoff slate (MIA, @CHI, HOU) is manageable and the wk11 bye is convenient.

c.j. stroud.verdict: Young, mobile passer with a top projection; consistency dipped but rushing floor is real
c.j. stroud.report: Stroud's PPG slid slightly from 13.0 to 12.3 but his 246 projection assumes a bounce-back with ~48-52 rushing attempts adding a floor. Ceiling is a return to efficient volume passing that lifts him into low-QB1 territory; floor is the 12 PPG steady he already delivers. He owns the HOU job outright (Mills, Mertz behind). Playoff draw of JAX, @PHI, @GB is mixed with two tough road spots in weeks 16-17.

sam darnold.verdict: 18 PPG in 2024 shows the ceiling; 2025 regression and SEA move add variance
sam darnold.report: Darnold exploded for 308 points (18.1 PPG) in 2024 then regressed to 235 (13.8) in 2025, so his 242 projection splits the difference at a new stop in Seattle. Ceiling is a repeat of that top-5 rushing-aided 2024 line (67 carries that year); floor is mid-teens with turnover risk given his career volatility. He's the clear SEA starter over Milroe and Lock. A wk15 @PHI matchup is rough but LAR and @CAR round out a usable playoff run.

bryce young.verdict: Ascending arc (11.5 to 12.8 PPG) plus 54 carries gives late-round upside
bryce young.report: Young improved his PPG from 11.5 to 12.8 while cutting weekly variance and adding rushing volume (54 carries), a genuine forward-trending profile at age. His 238 projection banks on continued growth; ceiling is a 15+ PPG breakout with the added legs, floor is the ~12 PPG floor he settled into. Only Pickett sits behind him on the CAR chart. Early wk5 bye and a fine CIN/@PIT/SEA playoff mix.

cam ward.verdict: Rookie-year 11 PPG with lowest variance in tier; sophomore leap is the bet
cam ward.report: Ward's rookie campaign (187 points, 11.0 PPG) came with the lowest weekly stdev (5.2) of any streamer here, showing steady if unspectacular output plus 39 carries. The 219 projection is conservative; ceiling is a second-year jump as the offense grows around him, floor is more of the same modest production. He's entrenched as TEN QB1 over Levis and Trubisky. Playoff schedule (IND, @LV, PIT) is neutral-to-favorable.

geno smith.verdict: 15.6 PPG in 2024 collapsed to 10.2 in 2025; new NYJ home caps the upside
geno smith.report: Geno's production cratered from 266 points (15.6 PPG) in 2024 to 174 (10.2) in 2025, and the 232 projection expects a partial rebound on the Jets. Ceiling is a return toward his 2024 form with the right supporting cast; floor is a repeat of the 2025 slump amplified by a weaker offense. He holds the job over Klubnik and Zappe but this is a clear age/decline situation. Wk13 bye and a workable @ARI/NE/MIN playoff run.

aaron rodgers.verdict: Steady 13.4 PPG but a 21-year vet with declining trend and a 218 projection
aaron rodgers.report: Rodgers dipped from 15.1 to 13.4 PPG year over year, and his 218 projection is the honest read on a 21st-season passer with minimal rushing. Ceiling is a healthy full slate of mid-teens output behind a competent PIT line; floor is an injury-shortened or further-declined season with Rudolph/Howard waiting. He's the starter but the depth chart signals the front office is planning ahead. Wk15 BAL is a tough playoff opener before easier CAR/@TEN games.

malik willis.verdict: 238 projection is pure speculation off two 3.0 PPG backup seasons; huge uncertainty
malik willis.report: Willis has produced just 3.0 PPG in each of the last two years as a spot backup, so the 238 projection entirely bets on him seizing and holding the MIA starting job. Ceiling is a mobile QB1 breakout if the offense leans on his legs; floor is being benched for Ewers by midseason and returning to irrelevance. That competition (Ewers, Miller) is a live threat to his snaps. A brutal wk17 BUF playoff matchup dents his tournament appeal.

fernando mendoza.verdict: Rookie with no NFL data and a 187 projection; Cousins looming behind him
fernando mendoza.report: Mendoza is a true rookie with zero prior production, so his 187 projection is a projection of raw talent into an uncertain LV situation. Ceiling is a Ward-like rookie contribution with rushing juice; floor is being pulled for veteran Cousins if he struggles early. That Cousins/O'Connell depth behind him is a real leash-shortener. Late wk13 bye and a fine DEN/TEN/@ARI playoff draw offer marginal streaming value.

deshaun watson.verdict: Listed as QB2 behind Sanders with a 124 projection; not draftable in standard leagues
deshaun watson.report: Watson's last data (4.5 PPG in 2024) was among the worst starter lines in the league, and he now sits behind Shedeur Sanders as CLE's QB2. The 124 projection assumes only spot duty; ceiling requires an injury ahead of him and even then his recent play offers little. Floor is essentially zero fantasy relevance on the bench. Purely a deep-league insurance flyer, not a stream.

tua tagovailoa.verdict: 115 projection and a Penix logjam signal a shrinking role; avoid outside deep formats
tua tagovailoa.report: Tua's production fell from 10.7 to 9.5 PPG with virtually no rushing (20 carries), and his 115 projection plus Penix sitting at #2 suggests a tenuous grip on the ATL job. Ceiling is a healthy full season of low-end passing volume; floor is injury or benching that ends his fantasy value early given his documented durability concerns. High weekly variance (7.7-10.2 stdev) makes even his good weeks unreliable. Not worth a bench spot in most leagues.

brandon aubrey.verdict: Elite leg with volume and range; only kicker worth drafting above streamer level
brandon aubrey.report: Aubrey has posted 187 and 185 points across two straight full seasons, a level no other kicker approaches consistently. His elite range gives him a per-game ceiling that stands alone, and the Cowboys offense keeps him in scoring position often. Floor is capped by weekly variance (6.1 stdev) but he's played all 17 games both years. Playoff slate is neutral with a manageable trio; he's the one K worth a mid-round tie-breaker pick.

cameron dicker.verdict: Steady, accurate, low-variance producer on a competitive Chargers offense
cameron dicker.report: Dicker delivered 176 then 167 points with the lowest stdev among top options, making him one of the most reliable weekly floors at the position. The Chargers offense supplies enough drives to keep him relevant every week. Ceiling is limited without Aubrey's range, but the consistency is real. Playoff schedule (SF, @MIA, KC) is fine and his early bye (wk7) means no playoff bye conflict.

ka'imi fairbairn.verdict: High-volume Houston leg with top-tier 2025 output but real variance
ka'imi fairbairn.report: Fairbairn jumped to 190 points in 2025 after 166 the prior year, showing his upside when the Texans stall in the red zone and settle for kicks. That 6.5 stdev is the highest here, meaning boom-bust weeks. He's a proven 17-game workhorse with a decade of experience. Playoff draw (@PHI, @GB) has some tough spots but he's a fine target after the top two.

jason myers.verdict: Big 2025 bounce-back but 2024 collapse shows the volatility risk
jason myers.report: Myers rebounded to a position-leading 195 points in 2025 after cratering to 136 in 2024, a swing that warns against expecting the high end. The Seahawks offense outlook drives his value and moderate stdev keeps weeks stable. Floor is a concern given the recent low. He's a reliable veteran with 17-game durability, but bank on the middle of his range rather than the peak.

harrison mevis.verdict: Landed the Rams job; strong offense boosts a limited sample
harrison mevis.report: Mevis played just 9 games in 2025 at 9.0 ppg with no 2024 data, so the projection leans on the Rams' high-scoring offense rather than track record. The upside is real if he holds the job in a top-tier scoring attack. The floor is murky given inexperience and small sample. Playoff slate (DAL, @SEA, @TB) is manageable; he's a speculative streamer-plus.

eddy pineiro.verdict: 49ers offense lifts a modest leg; volume-dependent upside
eddy pineiro.report: Pineiro improved to 139 points in 2025 from just 103 in 2024, benefiting from the 49ers offense generating chances. His higher stdev signals inconsistency and he missed a game in 2025. The ceiling depends entirely on SF staying healthy and driving into scoring range. Playoff road games (@LAC, @KC) are tougher; treat him as a mid-tier streamer.

cam little.verdict: Ascending young leg trending up two straight years
cam little.report: Little climbed from 124 to 162 points across his first two seasons, a clear upward trajectory as the Jaguars offense grows. He's played all 17 games both years and offers young-leg range. Floor sits around low streamer output if Jacksonville stalls. Playoff schedule (@HOU, @DAL, WSH) is neutral; a fine late-round upside bet.

jake bates.verdict: Low-variance Lions leg but touchdown-heavy offense caps kick volume
jake bates.report: Bates posted 158 then 145 points with the lowest stdev in the group, giving a stable but unexciting weekly line. The Lions' explosive offense often scores TDs rather than settling for field goals, which caps his ceiling. Durable across 17 games both seasons. Playoff draw is neutral; a safe floor play without much upside.

harrison butker.verdict: Name value outpaces recent output; KC scores TDs not FGs
harrison butker.report: Butker rebounded to 144 points in 2025 after a dismal 96 in 2024, but the Chiefs' red-zone efficiency limits his kick volume. His low stdev keeps weeks stable but unspectacular. The floor is solid given KC's consistent scoring, the ceiling capped without extra-point volume converting to field goals. Playoff slate (NE, SF, @LAC) is fine; a middling streamer.

tyler loop.verdict: Rookie holding Ravens job in a strong offense; unproven but promising
tyler loop.report: Loop delivered 140 points as a rookie across all 17 games, a solid debut in Baltimore's high-scoring attack. The upside is meaningful if the Ravens keep producing scoring drives. Floor carries second-year regression risk given the single-year sample. Playoff schedule (@PIT, @CIN) has divisional toughness but volume should carry him.

cairo santos.verdict: Improving Bears offense could lift a veteran leg with variance
cairo santos.report: Santos rose from 105 to 127 points as the Bears offense showed signs of life, but his output remains low-end and his 5.1 stdev adds bust weeks. The ceiling depends on Chicago's continued offensive improvement. Floor is streamer-level. Playoff draw (@BUF, GB, DET) is one of the tougher slates here; back-end option.

will reichard.verdict: Young Vikings leg trending up; volume tied to offensive health
will reichard.report: Reichard improved from 125 to 158 points in his second year with reduced variance, a good developmental sign. The Vikings offense determines his ceiling and there's upside if they field a competent passing game. Floor sits at low-end streamer if the offense sputters. Playoff schedule (DET, WSH, @NYJ) is manageable; a fine late flier.

chris boswell.verdict: Big 2024 crashed to average in 2025; age and offense concerns
chris boswell.report: Boswell fell from an elite 188 points in 2024 to just 147 in 2025, a steep drop that flags decline or offensive regression in Pittsburgh. His high stdev means volatile weeks. The ceiling exists given his 2024 peak but recent trend points down. Playoff slate (BAL, CAR, @TEN) is neutral; bank on the lower output.

chase mclaughlin.verdict: Consistent Bucs leg with solid two-year track record
chase mclaughlin.report: McLaughlin posted 162 then 151 points across two full seasons, a reliable mid-pack producer in Tampa's competent offense. Moderate variance keeps him usable most weeks. Ceiling is limited but the floor is steady. His draft rank slid to 240 despite fine production, offering late-round value; playoff slate (NO, @ATL, LAR) is workable.

evan mcpherson.verdict: High-variance Bengals leg; strong offense but inconsistent output
evan mcpherson.report: McPherson improved to 134 points in 2025 from a poor 88 in 2024, but his 5.9 stdev makes him a boom-bust weekly play. The Bengals' passing offense provides scoring-drive volume that gives real ceiling if he converts. Floor is shaky given the recent low. Playoff draw (@CAR, @IND, BAL) is mostly favorable; a lottery-ticket streamer.

nick folk.verdict: Ancient veteran with a low ceiling on a mediocre offense
nick folk.report: Folk climbed to 126 points in 2025 with the lowest variance around, but the ceiling is minimal on Atlanta's offense and he's 19 years into his career. The floor is stable thanks to accuracy. There's little upside to chase here. Playoff schedule (@WSH, TB, NO) is fine; strictly a late-round streamer.

trey smack.verdict: Rookie with no NFL data and a backup on roster; pure speculation
trey smack.report: Smack has zero pro data and faces Lucas Havrisik as listed competition, making his projection entirely conjecture. The Packers' strong offense provides upside if he wins and holds the job. The floor is a job-loss scenario, the widest downside here. Only draftable as a deep dart in the final rounds.

jake elliott.verdict: Declining output in a TD-heavy Eagles offense; lowest projection
jake elliott.report: Elliott dropped from 133 to just 109 points in 2025, the weakest recent trend as Philadelphia's offense scores TDs and reduces his field-goal chances. Low variance but low ceiling makes him a floor-only play. There's little reason to expect a rebound given the offensive profile. Playoff slate (SEA, HOU, @SF) is neutral; last-tier streamer.

texans d/st.verdict: Elite pass rush and takeaway unit, top projection and lowest variance among DSTs
texans d/st.report: Houston jumped from 8.2 PPG in 2024 to a strong 10.2 in 2025 while cutting weekly stdev to a remarkably low 3.7, signaling a reliable week-to-week floor rare for the position. The 128 projection leads the group and reflects a genuine top-tier defense built on pass rush and turnovers. Floor case is a consistent stream of respectable weeks; ceiling is elite if turnover luck spikes. Playoff slate is mixed with a soft JAX in wk15 but tougher road trips to PHI and GB in wks 16-17.

broncos d/st.verdict: Top-tier sack machine, consistent two-year producer with high projection
broncos d/st.report: Denver posted 9.8 then 8.5 PPG across the last two years, both strong with sack-heavy scoring, and carries the group's highest projection at 131. Weekly stdev around 6.1-6.4 is average, so expect some boom-bust but a solid overall floor. Ceiling is a league-winning sack total if the front stays healthy. Playoff schedule is favorable with @LV and @NE bookending a tougher BUF matchup in wk16.

seahawks d/st.verdict: Big 2025 leap to 10.9 PPG but high variance and tough wk15 at PHI
seahawks d/st.report: Seattle nearly doubled its output from 7.1 PPG in 2024 to a group-leading 10.9 in 2025, though the 8.2 weekly stdev is the highest here, flagging heavy boom-bust dependence. The 121 projection tempers expectations with regression baked in. Ceiling is elite in the right matchups; floor drags on quiet weeks against good offenses. Playoff draw is rough with @PHI in wk15, though @CAR in wk17 is a plus streaming spot.

rams d/st.verdict: Steady improvement and solid projection, decent playoff matchups
rams d/st.report: Los Angeles climbed from 5.9 to 7.4 PPG and the 123 projection suggests continued improvement behind a strong pass rush. Weekly stdev in the mid-5s is manageable for the position. Ceiling is a top-8 finish if the front generates consistent pressure; floor is streamer-level output. Playoff schedule offers a friendly wk15 DAL but road trips to SEA and TB later.

steelers d/st.verdict: Down year in 2025 but 126 projection banks on rebound, strong playoff slate
steelers d/st.report: Pittsburgh slipped to 6.6 PPG in 2025 from 7.9 with elevated 7.2 stdev, but the 126 projection reflects belief in a bounce-back behind their veteran defensive core. The unit remains capable of takeaway bursts. Ceiling is top-6 if the turnover rate normalizes upward; floor is inconsistent single-digit weeks. Playoff schedule is appealing with home CAR in wk16 and @TEN in wk17.

eagles d/st.verdict: Consistent low-variance unit but modest ceiling and tough wk17 at SF
eagles d/st.report: Philadelphia has been steady around 7.4-8.1 PPG with a controlled 5.1 stdev, offering a reliable if unspectacular floor. The 107 projection places it in the middle tier without breakout upside. Ceiling depends on their front driving sacks; floor is safe streamer territory. Playoff draw is neutral with SEA and HOU at home before a tricky @SF in wk17.

patriots d/st.verdict: Massive 2025 turnaround from 2.8 to 7.8 PPG signals a real unit
patriots d/st.report: New England exploded from a dreadful 2.8 PPG in 2024 to 7.8 in 2025, a legitimate signal of an improving defense rather than noise. The 100 projection is cautious given the short track record. Ceiling is a mid-tier weekly starter; floor risks reverting if the roster overhaul stalls. Playoff schedule is unfriendly with @KC in wk15 and @NYJ in wk16 before a home DEN game.

ravens d/st.verdict: Name-brand unit fell to 4.5 PPG but 118 projection expects strong rebound
ravens d/st.report: Baltimore cratered to 4.5 PPG in 2025 with a high 7.4 stdev after 6.2 the prior year, yet the 118 projection bets heavily on a talent-driven rebound. The pedigree and pass rush give real upside if health returns. Ceiling is top-8; floor is another disappointing takeaway-starved season. Playoff slate is divisional and tough with @PIT, CLE, @CIN.

lions d/st.verdict: Underwhelming production but 108 projection banks on offense-fueled game scripts
lions d/st.report: Detroit has hovered near 5.4-5.9 PPG the last two years, modest for a team that plays with leads and forces desperation passing. The 108 projection sees streaming value from positive game scripts. Ceiling is decent in favorable matchups; floor is fringe-startable. Playoff schedule mixes @MIN, home NYG, and @CHI, a manageable set.

browns d/st.verdict: Big jump to 8.4 PPG in 2025, favorable wk15 and wk17 matchups
browns d/st.report: Cleveland doubled output from 4.1 to 8.4 PPG in 2025, reflecting a strong defensive front that can carry despite offensive limitations. The 104 projection lags the actual but acknowledges variance. Ceiling is a top-10 sack unit; floor risks bad game scripts on a losing team. Playoff schedule helps with @NYG in wk15 and home IND in wk17 sandwiching a tough @BAL.

chargers d/st.verdict: Steady mid-single-digit producer, streamer with neutral schedule
chargers d/st.report: Los Angeles has been consistent at 6.9-7.0 PPG with average variance, a dependable stream-in option without top-tier upside. The 94 projection places it squarely in the back half. Ceiling is occasional big weeks; floor is replaceable production. Playoff slate features home SF and KC around a wk16 @MIA, mixed value.

vikings d/st.verdict: Solid 2025 but 72 projection signals sharp expected regression
vikings d/st.report: Minnesota produced 7.7 PPG in 2025 with a huge 8.6 stdev, yet the 72 projection is the lowest here, implying the model expects significant decline or scheme/personnel losses. That gap is a red flag for drafters. Ceiling is boom weeks if the pass rush holds; floor is bottom-tier. Playoff matchups include DET and @NYJ with a favorable WSH in wk16.

chiefs d/st.verdict: Low variance but muted ceiling, easy wk15 vs NE
chiefs d/st.report: Kansas City posted 5.2 PPG in 2025 with a tight 4.8 stdev, offering predictability but limited upside. The 100 projection expects a modest bounce. Ceiling is a fringe weekly starter; floor is streamer depth. Playoff schedule is favorable with home NE in wk15 before tougher SF and @LAC games.

packers d/st.verdict: Collapsed from 8.2 to 4.5 PPG, projection hopes for partial rebound
packers d/st.report: Green Bay fell hard from 8.2 PPG in 2024 to just 4.5 in 2025, and the 89 projection only partially restores confidence. The talent exists but the recent trend is discouraging. Ceiling is a return to 2024 form; floor is another lost year. Playoff schedule offers home MIA and HOU around @CHI.

jaguars d/st.verdict: Huge 2025 leap but 81 projection distrusts sustainability
jaguars d/st.report: Jacksonville surged from 2.1 PPG in 2024 to 8.2 in 2025, an enormous swing the 81 projection is skeptical of sustaining. Volatility makes this a risky season-long anchor. Ceiling is another surprise top-15 unit; floor is a reversion to weak takeaway output. Playoff schedule is mixed with @HOU, @DAL, and home WSH.

buccaneers d/st.report: Tampa Bay has been stuck around 5.2-5.4 PPG both years with high variance, offering little reason to draft over streaming. The 93 projection is optimistic relative to actuals. Ceiling is sporadic big weeks; floor is bench material. Playoff schedule features home NO in wk15 and LAR in wk17 with @ATL between.

colts d/st.verdict: Consistently weak producer, low-priority late pick
colts d/st.report: Indianapolis has managed just 4.4-4.8 PPG across two years with modest variance, marking it a bottom-tier fantasy unit. The 88 projection expects only marginal improvement. Ceiling is a few useful matchup weeks; floor is undraftable production. Playoff schedule includes @TEN and home CIN, streamable spots.

bears d/st.verdict: Flat 5.5 PPG output with high variance, streamer at best
bears d/st.report: Chicago has produced a steady but unexciting 5.5-5.6 PPG with elevated stdev, offering boom-bust weeks without a reliable floor. The 84 projection reflects low expectations. Ceiling is occasional turnover-driven spikes; floor is deep-bench. Playoff schedule is rough with @BUF in wk15 before home GB and DET.

bengals d/st.verdict: Cratered to 2.8 PPG in 2025, avoid outside deep matchup streams
bengals d/st.report: Cincinnati bottomed out at 2.8 PPG in 2025 from 5.5, one of the worst fantasy defenses, and the 85 projection is generous. This is a last-resort unit. Ceiling requires a full scheme turnaround; floor is negative-adjacent weeks. Playoff schedule offers a soft @CAR in wk15 but @IND and home BAL after.

49ers d/st.verdict: Injury-ravaged unit fell to 3.6 PPG, deep-league flyer only
49ers d/st.report: San Francisco dropped from 4.9 to a dismal 3.6 PPG in 2025, reflecting an injury-decimated defense that lost its former elite ceiling. The 82 projection assumes some health recovery. Ceiling is a return toward relevance if the front gets healthy; floor is bottom-of-league. Playoff schedule is brutal with @LAC, @KC, and home PHI.

jets d/st.verdict: Streamer-only DST with sharp production decline; playoff schedule offers NE matchup upside only
jets d/st.report: The Jets D/ST collapsed from a respectable 5.2 PPG in 2024 to just 1.9 PPG in 2025, a steep decline that signals eroding pass-rush and takeaway production heading into 2026. The ceiling case leans on a soft Week 16 matchup vs NE and generally streamable spots, but the floor is ugly given last year's near-worthless output. Both DSTs share the same 81 projection and near-identical ADP, so this is a coin-flip late-round dart. Draft neither before your final pick, and be ready to stream based on weekly matchups.

saints d/st.verdict: Higher recent output than Jets but tough playoff slate; still just a late streamer
saints d/st.report: New Orleans nearly doubled its scoring from 3.9 PPG in 2024 to 7.2 PPG in 2025 with lower weekly variance, making it the more reliable of these two on recent trend. The ceiling is a top-15 finish if the takeaway rate holds, but the floor is real given the difficult playoff schedule with road games @TB and @ATL bookending Week 16 vs ARI. Identical 81 projection and ADP to the Jets means this is purely a preference and matchup call. Grab it as a final-pick DST and monitor waivers for better weekly streams.
